To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students' assessments of their college's climate of concern are highly related to the aggregate characteristics of the student body, to the institutional structure, and to the faculty's characteristics; (2) the most powerful predictor of students' perceptions of their college environment is the proportion of faculty who are full-time, tenure-track, and in the social sciences; and (3) the most powerful predictors of faculty characteristics are the size of the student body and the proportion of faculty with doctorates in the
the most important determinants of students' assessments of their institution's college environment are the aggregate characteristics of students and the aggregate characteristics of faculty.
the most important factors in the college environment as perceived by the students are the students' own characteristics and the structural characteristics of the institution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degree to which students feel their college environment is one in which the faculty are concerned for them.
the relationship between the characteristics of students' college environment, and the characteristics of their faculty, and the institutional structure within which they work.
the question of how students perceive their college environment and the extent to which this perception is related to the characteristics of the institution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the college environment, as assessed by the students, is a product of the institutional characteristics, as well as the characteristics of the student population, but not of the “quality” of the faculty.
the more students are of the “traditional” type, the more they perceive the institution to be concerned for their welfare.

the college environment is a product of institutional structure, and that the faculty's role in the creation of that environment is largely a function of their institutional location, not a function of their individual characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more students are exposed to faculty who have high levels of commitment and who are concerned about their students, the more likely they will be to perceive a positive environment.

students' perceptions of their institutional environment are strongly affected by the aggregate characteristics of the institution and its faculty, and that these perceptions do not appear to be affected by the “quality” of the institution's faculty as traditionally measured.

the most important variables affecting the college environment as students perceive it are those measuring the institutional structure, the aggregate student body characteristics, and the aggregate faculty composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students’ perceptions of the college environment are strongly influenced by the composition and characteristics of the faculty and institutional structural features.

, in the absence of a more direct measure of faculty quality, the institutional structure and the student body characteristics are the best predictors of students’ perceptions of their college climate of care.
students' perceptions of their college environment are highly correlated with the characteristics of their institutions, as well as with the aggregate characteristics of their fellow students.
